steps.title: Exam Tip
steps.body: Some Christians are concerned that Christmas has become too commercialised — the focus on presents and Santa Claus can overshadow the birth of Jesus. Churches work to keep the religious meaning central through nativity services, carol concerts and Advent reflections.

steps.title: RS Exam Tips — Christmas and Easter
steps.body: 1. For Christmas and Easter questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of Christmas and Easter to its real-world impact on believers and society

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain why Easter is the most important Christian festival. | Explain two ways Christians celebrate Christmas.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Easter is the most important festival because it celebrates the resurrection — the event on which the entire Christian faith depends. Without the resurrection, Jesus would be just a dead teacher, and  | 1) Many Christians attend a Midnight Mass or Christmas Day service, which includes nativity readings from Luke's Gospel, carols, and a celebration of Jesus' birth. 2) Christians set up nativity scenes

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always refer to specific sources of authority (scripture, sacred texts, religious leaders) Explain contrasting beliefs — different views within and between traditions Use key terminology precisely (e.g. tawhid, atonement, sanctity of life) For 12-mark evaluation questions, consider both sides before reaching a justified conclusion Link beliefs to their impact on individuals, communities and society Acknowledge diversity — no religious tradition has a single, uniform view
